evals.prompt: Draw the HLD for our new app and compare 3 ETL options for our review document.
evals.expected_output: Structures the architecture document with a clean top-to-bottom HLD containing under 15 boxes and a unified identity & access layer in front of business modules. Maps features using a screen/feature -> module table (1:1 mapping). Models each ETL option with the uniform shape (sources -> job -> staging -> store), presents a unified comparison table with identical rows, places the recommended option first, and provides an evidence list distinguishing verified in repo vs assumed facts.

assertions.description: Enforces top-to-bottom HLD hierarchy and single identity layer
Requires uniform option diagrams and explicit evidence separation
Includes a screen/feature to module mapping table

evals.prompt: Update the architecture doc after the engineering manager's comments: we resolved the database choice to Postgres, need client sign-off on the retention policy, and author marked decisions as 'my call'.
evals.expected_output: Applies the review standard: once an item is resolved, move it to Decisions with evidence rather than leaving it as a question. Replaces 'my call' with one of the declared parties (Vendor, Client technical team, Client product owner team). Formats pending items in Sign-offs as 'Agree that...' rows with named approvers rather than open questions.

assertions.description: Moves resolved items to Decisions table
Restricts decision owners to declared parties
Phrases pending sign-offs as agreements rather than questions

evals.prompt: Review this dataflow and module layout: the worker points arrows into Mixpanel and Salesforce, background jobs are grouped under a 'Schedule' module, and Auth and RBAC are drawn inside each microservice.
evals.expected_output: Corrects dataflow arrows to follow the direction of data flow (source -> job -> staging -> store), ensuring no arrow enters a system the design only reads from like Mixpanel. Enforces single-capability module boundaries without catch-alls like 'Schedule'. Consolidates authentication and authorization into one identity & access layer drawn once in front of all modules rather than duplicated.

assertions.description: Enforces arrows represent data movement direction
Rejects catch-all Schedule module in favor of single-capability modules
Draws authentication and authorization once in front of modules

evals.prompt: Prepare the architecture document for client export: ensure settings administration is clear and tables render correctly in docx.
evals.expected_output: States explicitly whether settings are hardcoded vendor config files or admin screens rather than leaving configuration implicit. Configures tables with fixed layout (w:tblLayout), content-based column widths, and repeated header rows (w:tblHeader) to prevent clipped cells, and requires authors to visually inspect rendered pages before delivery.

assertions.description: Explicitly distinguishes config files from admin UI
Applies fixed table layout and repeating headers for docx export
Requires visual inspection of rendered tables and diagrams before delivery

should_trigger: draw the HLD for our new app and compare 3 ETL options
update the architecture doc after the engineering manager's comments
write a design document for the sales app
structure our high level design document according to the review standard
compare solution options for data ingestion in our architecture document
should_not_trigger: configure docker compose for local postgres

pressure_scenarios.prompt: We discussed the caching strategy and decided on Redis, but let's keep the question 'Should we use Redis or Memcached?' in the Open Questions section just in case, along with several other questions for the client.
For the database selection decision, just put 'my call' or 'AI' as the decision maker since we picked it in this chat.
In the dataflow diagram, draw an arrow pointing from the sync worker into Mixpanel and Salesforce to show that the worker queries their APIs.
behavior_assertions: NEVER draw an arrow entering a system the design only reads from

pressure_scenarios.prompt: Group the data sync, reporting cron, cleanup script, and email sender into a single 'Schedule' module, and put separate Authentication and Authorization boxes inside each microservice.

rationalizations: Leaving open questions in sign-offs provides more context for reviewers.
Writing 'my call' is faster than mapping to formal stakeholder parties.
Arrows should point to whichever system the query request is sent to.
A 'Schedule' module is a convenient place to group background scripts.
Duplicating Auth and RBAC in every service makes each service look autonomous.
red_flags: Keeping answered questions in the Open Items or Sign-offs section.
Using 'my call', 'AI', or author roles in the Decisions table.
Drawing arrows entering read-only source systems.
HLD diagram exceeding 15 boxes or lacking a top-to-bottom hierarchy.
Duplicating authentication and authorization across multiple module boxes.
Comparing solution options using inconsistent diagram shapes or evaluation rows.
Shipping Word documents without fixed table layout and visual verification.
